claim: For the Memarzadeh--Mancini channel restricted to the qutrit Fock space \(\operatorname{span}\{|0\rangle,|1\rangle,|2\rangle\}\), impose the mean-energy constraint \(N=3/2\) and take pure dephasing \(\epsilon=1\). For every \(0<t\le \log(4/3)\), the admissible adjacent-level state \(|\chi\rangle=(|1\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2\) has strictly smaller output von Neumann entropy than every candidate allowed by Conjecture 1 of Memarzadeh and Mancini (2016): the unique admissible binomial state, with \(M=2\) and \(\mu=3/4\), and every phase-equivalent endpoint state \(|\kappa_\alpha\rangle=\tfrac12|0\rangle+\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}e^{2i\alpha}|2\rangle\). Hence Conjecture 1 is false already in dimension three, and in fact fails on the whole nontrivial interval \(0<t\le\log(4/3)\).

integrity.computational_dependence: none for the theorem; bundled rational checker verifies algebraic identities
integrity.prior_work_preserved: the channel definition, candidate families, and conjecture are attributed to Memarzadeh and Mancini; later capacity results are treated as distinct objectives
integrity.proof_type: exact symbolic entropy comparison via purity and largest-eigenvalue bounds

scientific_limitations: The counterexample is proved for pure dephasing, the qutrit truncation, mean energy 3/2, and 0<t<=log(4/3).
It disproves the candidate-family conjecture but does not identify the global minimizer outside the proved interval or parameter slice.
A differently phrased later counterexample may exist outside the literature surfaced by the recorded searches.
title: Adjacent-level qutrit counterexamples to a truncated non-Gaussian minimum-output-entropy conjecture
